SRC-371:R001.text: FORENSIC INVENTORY OF EVERY CURRENT STAGED ENTRY Before any mutation, obtain a consistent read-only snapshot of the real live index and Git metadata. Capture the exact index bytes/hash, HEAD, branch, push remote, worktree identity, Git object identities and concurrent-writer context. Enumerate staged entries using machine-readable, NUL-delimited Git output (including status v2, cached raw/name-status, ls-files --stage, and unmerged stages where relevant). Correctly handle renames, copies, deletions, modes, symlinks, Git LFS, submodules, conflict stages, Unicode names and Windows path peculiarities. Do not parse human-readable git status as an authoritative machine manifest. Create a durable, reviewable per-entry evidence inventory with: - exact path(s) and staged operation; - index blob object ID and mode; - working-tree and HEAD relationship; - commit ancestry and applicable branch; - evidence of producer/owner (ticket, source, release scope, host, user or other project); - review status and verification scope; - release destination eligibility; - secret/private content risk; - classification and reason. Classify each entry as one of: SAIPEN_OWNED_REVIEWED SAIPEN_OWNED_UNREVIEWED OTHER_TICKET_OR_COHORT FOREIGN_PROJECT_OR_OWNER GENERATED_OR_TRANSIENT SENSITIVE_OR_PUBLICATION_FORBIDDEN AMBIGUOUS_PROVENANCE Use current evidence to determine ownership. Absence from one ticket's scope is not proof of foreign ownership. Git blame, filenames, timestamps, or a model's assertion alone cannot establish authority. If the original number is wrong, report the actual number and why it changed.

SRC-371:R002.text: REMOVE THE FALSE GLOBAL BLOCKER Determine whether the canonical blocker is caused by unclassified pre-staged paths, shared-index mutability, absent reviewed scope, failed release gates, unavailable signed approval, or multiple independent causes. Do not demand that the operator choose what to do with individual files. Choose the safest supported technical strategy automatically: - Leave original staged and unstaged user state untouched. - Put only attributable, reviewed SAIPEN-owned release paths in a separate canonical worktree/index. - Keep other-ticket/cohort paths linked to their original owners, not absorbed into a random release. - Preserve genuinely foreign, unreviewed, ambiguous, sensitive and forbidden entries without alteration. - Do not require the entire shared index to become empty before independent release work can proceed. Do not run git reset, clean, stash, force checkout, blanket add, destructive rebase, or a whole-tree commit. Do not transfer source-owned changes without proving path containment, source revision and authorized scope. Preserve rename pairs and deletions correctly. If a safe independent release can be prepared, finish its machine-verifiable work regardless of unrelated staging.

SRC-371:R003.text: RECONCILE EXISTING RELEASES WITHOUT REPLAY Inspect prior isolated-release attempts, aborted plans, pending cohorts, exact approved scopes, release receipts, local commits and remote branch/tag state. Do not start a duplicate transaction merely because a status says WAIT. If the intended exact release commit is already on the verified destination, record the correct synchronized receipt and avoid a no-op push. If a different cohort remains pending, do not claim it was published because an older remote SHA matches. For any genuinely new approved release: validate current tree, selected scope, required test evidence, exact destination and branch, non-fast-forward safety, secret/public visibility, authorization and rollback. Run mandatory publication gates against the exact final release bytes. Compare the independently observed remote SHA to the exact expected commit, not merely to a changed remote tip. The existing release engine and broker remain authoritative. A model handoff is not a signed broker receipt, and a native host hook is not necessarily a human publication approval. If exact authorization is absent, persist RELEASE_READY_AWAITING_AUTHORITY with one complete, scope-bound approval packet. Do not forge, weaken, or reuse mismatched grants. Preserve the primary index even if approval is unavailable.

SRC-371:R004.text: FIX THE PRODUCTION DECISION PATH, NOT JUST THIS INCIDENT Trace the actual classifier and host response path that converts "staging outside current ticket" into global WAIT_USER_DECISION or NEXT EXACT ACTION: NONE. Add durable ownership projection and safe independent-release routing to existing canonical modules, rather than another parallel release framework. Release authorization blocks RELEASE only; it must not block independent, already-authorized engineering, evidence gathering, HUNT, Improve, SAIPAL discovery or verification. However, do not perform protected mutations when the current grant is expired or lacks the necessary scope. Keep authority and queue/objective state separate. After a successful release or a precisely isolated release blocker, resume independently eligible work through the existing persistent goal/campaign runner. Do not manufacture tickets to avoid idleness. If no legitimate work remains, enter event-driven quiescence with an exact wake condition. Do not recommend unchanged saipen status as if it were progress.

SRC-371:R005.text: NON-INVASIVE REGRESSION AND ACCEPTANCE Use disposable repositories and isolated worktrees for destructive tests. Routine tests must not capture foreground focus, mouse, keyboard, or active desktop windows. Required negative and positive controls: - historical count differs from current index count; - a staged file belongs to SAIPEN but a different ticket; - a staged file belongs to a genuine foreign owner; - ambiguous provenance is preserved rather than adopted; - staged rename, deletion, mode-only change and unmerged conflict; - symlink/junction/traversal escape and Windows path collision; - concurrently changing original index: detect, do not overwrite or restore over writer; - isolated worktree excludes every unreviewed/foreign entry; - failed release does not mutate or erase original staged bytes; - release plan becomes stale and is safely rebuilt; - previous cohort already synchronized and new cohort still pending; - wrong remote, unsafe visibility, non-fast-forward and force-push refusal; - stale full-suite evidence cannot approve changed release bytes; - valid exact-scope broker receipt passes, missing/forged receipt refuses; - unrelated authorized Work continues while release is blocked; - no duplicate commit, tag or push after crash or retry; - verified remote commit matches expected exact SHA. Independently verify the original index integrity before and after any allowed isolated operation. Distinguish contract tests from real installed-host and remote acceptance. Avoid unnecessary large full-suite reruns during source edits, but honor the required final release gate.

SRC-371:R006.text: EXECUTION ORDER A. Preserve any current DOING Work and authoritative ownership. B. Inventory all actual live staged entries read-only. C. Build a per-file provenance and release-eligibility ledger. D. Group entries into exact owner/cohort categories with justified evidence. E. Reconcile prior release operations and the real remote state. F. Implement a safe isolated route for the reviewed, eligible subset. G. Add failing regression controls for any reproduced blocker and fix its root cause. H. Run focused and affected tests, then the mandatory exact-release gate. I. If already authorized, execute and verify the intended release; otherwise prepare one exact broker approval request while preserving the shared index. J. Resume independently authorized self-maintenance rather than returning to a global WAIT. SUCCESS IS NOT "206 files cleared." Success is that every current staged entry is accounted for, nothing unowned is damaged, eligible releases are no longer held hostage by unrelated staging, the remote release state is truthful, and authorized engineering can continue. FINAL REPORT (CONCISE USER STATUS; DETAILED MANIFEST IN PROJECT EVIDENCE) LIVE_STAGED_COUNT: INDEX_IDENTITY_BEFORE/AFTER: SAIPEN_OWNED_REVIEWED: SAIPEN_OWNED_UNREVIEWED: OTHER_COHORT: GENUINELY_FOREIGN: GENERATED_OR_SENSITIVE: AMBIGUOUS: PER_FILE_MANIFEST_PATH: ROOT_CAUSE_OF_SHARED_INDEX_WAIT: EXISTING_RELEASE_RECONCILIATION: ISOLATED_COHORT: FULL_RELEASE_GATE: EXPECTED_REMOTE_SHA: OBSERVED_REMOTE_SHA: PUBLICATION_AUTHORITY: RELEASE_OUTCOME: ORIGINAL_INDEX_PRESERVED: INDEPENDENT_ENGINEERING_PROGRESS: EXACT_REMAINING_BLOCKER: NEXT_LAWFUL_ACTION: NEXT_WAKE_CONDITION: Do not return another generic "foreign staging: operator decision required" without this real inventory and a proven isolated strategy. Do not pretend that technical delegation is a broker-signed publication permission. Implement what is authorized; preserve what is not; continue useful independent work. END SAIHANDOFF
